title: How many matchsticks are needed for a step far down the pattern?
description: A row of matchstick triangles grows by two matchsticks at every step, starting with three in Step one. The board counts how many twos are added to reach Step five, thirty three, eighty four and one hundred and eight. Keeko's doubt is that Step thirty three has thirty three times two matchsticks.
teaching_notes: One idea: a step far down the pattern is the starting three plus the twos added since Step one, and one fewer two than the step number is added. Watch for students who multiply the step number by two and forget the starting three.

source: Find the number of matchsticks in Step 5, Step 33, Step 84 a
video_script.why: A learner finds matchsticks in a far step by adding the repeated twos to the starting three.
video_script.substitution: the book's matchstick triangles, Step one has three matchsticks and each step adds two
video_script.anchor: the book's row of matchstick triangles, one more triangle at each step
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko multiplies the step number by two. Step one would have two matchsticks, but Step one has three, so the count starts at three and adds a two at every later step.

final_answer.spoken: eleven, sixty seven, one hundred and sixty nine and two hundred and seventeen matchsticks

maths_rules: counts 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 grow by 2 at each step
Step 33: 32 twos are added, so 3 + 2 x 32 = 3 + 64 = 67
Keeko test: 1 x 2 = 2 but Step 1 has 3
video_script.design: The first steps of the triangle pattern stay on the board with a table of the counts. The twos added are counted for each far step.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a pattern made with matchsticks.
<bookmark mark='steps'/>Step one has one triangle, Step two has two triangles, and Step three has three triangles.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We can draw the next steps, but how can we find Step thirty three without drawing?

beats.on_screen: the matchstick pattern stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: table: Step 1 to 6 with matchsticks 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 ; each step adds 2

marks.table: the table of counts is filled

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one needs three matchsticks.
<bookmark mark='add'/>To get the next step, two more matchsticks are placed.
<bookmark mark='table'/>The counts go three, five, seven, nine, eleven, thirteen, growing by two each time.

beats.on_screen: Given: Step 1 has 3 matchsticks ; each step adds 2

marks.gv: the starting count and the added two are written

narration: <bookmark mark='gv'/>Given, Step one has three matchsticks, and every step adds two more.

beats.on_screen: To find: the matchsticks in Step 5, Step 33, Step 84 and Step 108
narration: <bookmark mark='fd'/>We have to find the matchsticks in four steps. They are Step five, Step thirty three, Step eighty four and Step one hundred and eight.

marks.list: the counts are listed up to Step 5

narration: <bookmark mark='list'/>First, for Step five, keep adding two to the count. Three, five, seven, nine, eleven.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Step five has eleven matchsticks.

marks.count: 32 twos are marked, one fewer than 33

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Second, Step thirty three starts at three. It adds two thirty two times, because Step one needs no two.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Three plus two times thirty two is three plus sixty four, which is sixty seven.
<bookmark mark='s84'/>Third, Step eighty four adds eighty three twos.
<bookmark mark='r84'/>Three plus two times eighty three is three plus one hundred and sixty six. That is one hundred and sixty nine.
<bookmark mark='s108'/>Step one hundred and eight adds one hundred and seven twos. Three plus two hundred and fourteen is two hundred and seventeen.

marks.ans: the first two answers are boxed
marks.ans2: the last two answers are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Step five needs eleven matchsticks, and Step thirty three needs sixty seven. <bookmark mark='ans2'/>Step eighty four needs one hundred and sixty nine. Step one hundred and eight needs two hundred and seventeen.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the matchstick pattern
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: Step 33 = 33 × 2, struck out ; Step 1 would give 1 × 2 = 2 but has 3

marks.test: Step 1 is tested: 1 × 2 = 2 but the picture shows 3
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and 3 + 2 × 32 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks Step thirty three has thirty three times two matchsticks.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Test the idea on Step one. One times two is two, but Step one has three.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The count starts at three, and a two is added for every step after the first.
